items.title: Index and LSP authority are explicitly separated
items.statement: The code index remains an independent per-project, indexer-backed, watcher-driven state owner; it feeds search, while per-file LSP sessions attach through the editor lifecycle and feed editing intelligence.

evidence.exact_quote: - The code index remains a SEPARATE `/state-owning` subsystem from LSP: it is per-project, `/indexer` backed, watcher-driven, and useful for large-workspace navigation even when LSP is disabled, unavailable, or degraded; per-file LSP sessions attach through the editor document lifecycle and feed editing, diagnostics, semantic navigation, and code-action context. Index feeds search; LSP feeds editing.

items.title: Fallback must disclose reduced capability
items.statement: When LSP is unavailable, navigation falls back to index/text search and heuristic or regex outline where possible, with optional install guidance, but cannot claim diagnostics, semantic features, or healthy attachment.

evidence.exact_quote: - When LSP is unavailable, Puppet Master falls back to code index/text search, `/regex` or heuristic outline where available, and optional `/download` or install hints. The fallback path must not claim diagnostics, semantic features, or healthy attached-server state.

items.title: Editor and protocol ownership are allocated
items.statement: FileManager owns the visible editor surface and named semantic affordances; LSPSupport owns protocol and client constraints, while Problems owns aggregated diagnostic presentation.

evidence.exact_quote: - The FileManager editor-surface map is explicit for LSP consumers: `§10.1 Breadcrumbs / outline` owns the breadcrumb strip and outline, with LSP using `documentSymbol` and fallback using heuristic / regex outline; `§10.2 Go to symbol` owns command-palette and quick-open symbols, with LSP using `documentSymbol` and `workspace/symbol`, while the legacy `§12.1.4` name survives only as a compatibility pointer to this fallback rule. `§10.10 LSP support (MVP)` is the editor-side owner for diagnostics, hover, completion, signature help, inlay hints, code actions, code lens, semantic highlighting, definition/references, `/rename/applyEdit`, format, `document/workspace symbols`, editor/chat adjacency, and the finer `§10.10.5`, `§10.10.6`, `§10.10.7`, and `§10.10.8` responsibility split. FileManager remains the visible editor owner; LSPSupport owns the LSP protocol/client constraints.
- diagnostics feed editor markers and Problems, but Problems remains the owner of aggregated problem presentation

items.title: Chat LSP is a shared-instance read-only intelligence surface
items.statement: Chat activates LSP intelligence only for a project-associated thread with running servers, analyzes code blocks by detected language, exposes completion, resolution, hover, and definition, remains read-only, and reuses editor server instances.

evidence.exact_quote: - Chat LSP activates when a chat thread has an associated project with LSP servers running
- Chat LSP provides read-only intelligence only; no refactoring and no code actions are exposed through this surface
- it uses the same LSP server instances as the editor rather than spawning a separate chat-only server pool

items.title: Diagnostic-to-chat payload and mutation boundary are specified
items.statement: Chat consumes the shared diagnostic entry shape plus session and URI references, preserves four severity labels, and any later mutation-capable workflow must preview, confirm, and apply through FileSafe-backed workspace/applyEdit.

evidence.exact_quote: Diagnostic-to-chat pipeline behavior is a context-packaging contract, not a second diagnostics owner. The `to-chat` payload uses the same diagnostic entry shape as §17.2 (`path`, `line`, `character`, `severity`, `message`, `source`, optional `code`) plus refs to the originating LSP session and URI; severity mapping preserves `Error`, `Warning`, `Info`, and `Hint` labels when chat summarizes or filters diagnostics. Chat LSP remains read-only for MVP; when a separate later-phase chat workflow surfaces a quick fix, code action, rename, or workspace edit from this diagnostic context, it opens explicit preview/confirmation and applies only through FileSafe-backed `workspace/applyEdit`, preserving the code action approval flow rather than mutating directly from the message.

items.title: Registration-before-spawn lifecycle is ordered
items.statement: A session record keyed by host, server, and root must enter starting under the session-map write lock before subprocess creation, then transition to ready or failed after handshake completion; background startup is lifecycle-tracked before spawn.

evidence.exact_quote: An LSP server MUST be registered in the session map (keyed by `(host_id, server_id, root_identity)`) before its process is spawned. Spawning before registration creates a window where the process exists but cannot be found, tracked, or shut down.
5. Transition the record to `ready` or `failed` after handshake completion.

items.title: Spawn failure cannot leave an occupied starting slot
items.statement: A post-registration spawn failure must either clean up the session record or mark it failed.

evidence.exact_quote: If spawn fails after registration, the session record is cleaned up or marked `failed` so the slot does not remain permanently occupied.

items.title: Crash recovery policy leaves a user-action versus auto-restart branch
items.statement: The crash mitigation specifies state cleanup and UI refresh, but permits either a manual restart button or automatic exponential-backoff restart. It does not choose the normative mode, define an attempt ceiling, or state the terminal state after repeated restart failures.
items.impact: Independent builders can implement materially different recovery behavior and user control semantics.
items.builder_discretion: Choose manual-only restart or automatic restart, plus retry ceiling and exhausted state.

evidence.exact_quote: | **Server crash or exit** | **Client (LSP layer):** On process exit or broken pipe (e.g. when writing to stdin fails), (1) mark that server's state as Error, (2) clear all diagnostics for documents owned by that server (DiagnosticsCache), (3) notify UI to refresh Problems panel and gutter. **UI:** Show "Error" in status bar for that server; offer "Restart language server" button (or auto-restart with exponential backoff, e.g. 1s, 2s, 4s, cap 30s). **Logging:** Log exit code and stderr tail for debugging. |

items.title: Open-document resource policy is exemplary rather than deterministic
items.statement: The document limit may be open tabs or N-most-recent documents and the Settings cap is optional with an example value, leaving selection order, default cap, per-root enforcement, and eviction behavior under-specified.
items.impact: Server memory pressure and didOpen/didClose behavior can vary substantially across implementations and large workspaces.
items.builder_discretion: Choose the eligibility set, recency algorithm, default N, and whether the cap exists.

evidence.exact_quote: | **Many open documents** | **Client:** Limit documents pushed to each server (e.g. only currently open tabs, or N most recent per root). **Editor/FileManager:** When a buffer is evicted (FileManager §12.2.1), **client** sends `didClose` for that URI so the server can free memory. **Config:** Optional cap (e.g. max 50 open docs per server) in Settings. |

items.title: Canonical tool inventory and approval boundary are normalized
items.statement: The canonical tool surface is nine read-only operations and one write-gated rename; lsp_rename is only a legacy alias, workspaceSymbol requires query, position operations use path and position, and rename additionally requires newName and approval.

evidence.exact_quote: - LSP canon must preserve the exact MVP operation inventory, normalized parameter shapes, and result envelope. The canonical tool surface is nine read-only operations plus one write/approval-gated `rename`; the packetization label `10 read-only + 1 write-gated (lsp_rename)` is reconciled here by treating `lsp_rename` as a legacy alias for `rename`, not a second operation. `workspaceSymbol` must carry `query`, position-based operations use `path` + `position`, and `rename` / `lsp_rename` requires `path` + `position` + `newName` with approval gating.

items.title: Operation result envelope defines status but not payloads
items.statement: The canonical operation contract enumerates input fields and a four-value status, but this section does not define per-operation result payload fields, partial-result semantics, unavailable/error details, or stable result identity.
items.impact: Tool callers, GUI consumers, and AI-context consumers cannot implement or validate interoperable results from this canonical surface alone.
items.builder_discretion: Invent result bodies, error metadata, and the meaning of partial for each operation.

evidence.exact_quote: - `obl-064` owns this MVP LSP features summary and requires the missing-result envelope `status: ok | partial | unavailable | error`; stale aliases, short names, or ad hoc result envelopes are retired in favor of this section.

Fields:
- operation
- query
- path
- position
- newName
- status

items.title: MVP transport boundary is explicit
items.statement: The MVP client speaks stdio only, including when it launches a bridge; native TCP/socket support is out of scope and the bridge pattern must be documented.

evidence.exact_quote: - **MVP:** Client talks stdio only (spawn server process, or spawn a bridge that talks stdio to us and TCP/other to the real server).

- **Native TCP/socket:** **Out of scope for MVP.** No implementation required. Implementer must document the bridge pattern only (e.g. Godot via godot-lsp-stdio-bridge). Later (optional): native TCP client for already-running servers; lower priority.

items.title: Phase outcomes provide user-visible milestone oracles
items.statement: Phase 1 requires usable files, diagnostics in editor and Problems, hover, completion, status, and fallback; Phase 2 requires the full listed editor LSP surface plus Chat LSP, Settings, timeouts, and fallbacks.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Phase 1 outcome:** User can open files, see diagnostics in editor and Problems panel, get hover and completion; status bar shows LSP state; fallback when no server.

- **Phase 2 outcome:** Full editor LSP (definition, references, rename, format, code actions, code lens, signature help, inlay hints); Chat has LSP-aware @ symbol, code-block hover/definition, Problems link; Settings > LSP and fallbacks in place.

items.title: Settings registry states and controls are concrete
items.statement: Settings > LSP is a searchable, filterable registry with master and per-server enablement, custom-server CRUD, override/reset behavior, requested-versus-effective state, validation, provenance, scope, lifecycle, install, and platform detail.

evidence.exact_quote: - `Settings > LSP lists all servers and custom entries with validation`; that phrase is a product requirement, not a placeholder. The GUI includes a global master toggle, a searchable `/filterable` full-catalog list, per-server enable/disable, add custom server `/form`, edit custom server action, `/built-in` override/reset behavior, malformed command/config validation, visible distinction among catalog/built-in server, built-in server with user override, user-added custom server, disabled/enabled/misconfigured/unavailable states, command plus args, handled extensions/selectors, env/init options, root-discovery mode, install `/provisioning` notes, and global vs project-scope override. Requested state and effective state must both be shown when a global enablement is masked by a project override or missing binary.

items.title: Custom-server validation lacks pass/fail and persistence semantics
items.statement: The GUI must validate malformed command/config and show validation errors, but the reviewed contract does not define validation timing, blocking versus warning classes, executable/path checks, save behavior on invalid data, or project/global conflict resolution errors.
items.impact: Different Settings implementations can accept incompatible or unsafe records and report effective state inconsistently.
items.builder_discretion: Choose validation rules, timing, severity, and whether invalid entries may be saved or enabled.

evidence.exact_quote: - `Settings > LSP lists all servers and custom entries with validation`; that phrase is a product requirement, not a placeholder. The GUI includes a global master toggle, a searchable `/filterable` full-catalog list, per-server enable/disable, add custom server `/form`, edit custom server action, `/built-in` override/reset behavior, malformed command/config validation, visible distinction among catalog/built-in server, built-in server with user override, user-added custom server, disabled/enabled/misconfigured/unavailable states, command plus args, handled extensions/selectors, env/init options, root-discovery mode, install `/provisioning` notes, and global vs project-scope override. Requested state and effective state must both be shown when a global enablement is masked by a project override or missing binary.

items.title: Cross-surface ownership and health disclosure are explicit
items.statement: File Manager/editor consume semantic state, Search owns text search and replace, Problems owns aggregated diagnostics, and status surfaces must expose freshness, health, and effective capability.

evidence.exact_quote:
- File Manager and editor consume LSP state for semantic affordances
- Search remains the owner of text search and replace-in-files
- Problems remains the owner of aggregated diagnostics display
- status surfaces disclose freshness, health, and effective capability state rather than hiding degraded attach conditions

items.title: Worktree identity and lifecycle are bound independently of focus
items.statement: Sessions use canonical on-host worktree paths, start per missing host/server/worktree key, shut down when the worktree is removed, coexist across worktrees, and persist across thread switches because lifecycle follows worktree existence rather than focus.

evidence.exact_quote: LSP sessions are keyed by `(host_id, server_id, root_identity)`. When a file belongs to a worktree rather than the main project root, the LSP root_identity MUST use the canonical on-host worktree path, not a raw path copied across hosts.
- LSP session lifecycle is tied to worktree existence, not thread focus

items.title: Worktree warm-start is non-normative
items.statement: Missing worktree sessions must start on demand, but proactive warm-start is conditioned on feasibility without defining feasibility, ownership, or resource limits.
items.impact: Startup latency and background resource use can differ among conforming implementations.
items.builder_discretion: Decide whether and when worktree creation triggers warm-start.

evidence.exact_quote: - If an LSP session for `(host_id, server_id, worktree_path)` does not exist, one is started (warm-start on worktree creation if feasible)

items.title: Environment values and stderr logging lack secret-handling rules
items.statement: The reviewed core requires configurable environment fields and crash logging of stderr tails, but supplies no redaction, secret-reference, storage, display-masking, or log-retention contract for sensitive values that may appear in either surface.
items.impact: Server tokens or credentials can be persisted or exposed through Settings and diagnostic logs inconsistently.
items.builder_discretion: Choose secret storage, masking, redaction, and retention behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: | **Server crash or exit** | **Client (LSP layer):** On process exit or broken pipe (e.g. when writing to stdin fails), (1) mark that server's state as Error, (2) clear all diagnostics for documents owned by that server (DiagnosticsCache), (3) notify UI to refresh Problems panel and gutter. **UI:** Show "Error" in status bar for that server; offer "Restart language server" button (or auto-restart with exponential backoff, e.g. 1s, 2s, 4s, cap 30s). **Logging:** Log exit code and stderr tail for debugging. |

- The LSP registry participates in the GUI Settings `/inspectors` pattern and the `two-level` Settings navigation model. Registry `/filtering` and `/filter/grouping` cover at least `/ecosystem`, language, source, requested state, effective state, support classification, and lifecycle state. Detail panes show canonical `/names`, aliases/source names, `/install/download/legal` and `/provisioning` posture, platform restrictions, command/env/init fields, and validation errors without turning Settings into the SSOT for runtime attachment.

items.title: Legacy navigation references have a migration route
items.statement: Named stale section anchors are explicitly legacy residue, and consumers must route to current FileManager section 10 or this LSPSupport section while preserving the specified fallback obligations.

evidence.exact_quote: - Stale references to `FileManager.md §12.1.4`, `§12.1.4`, `§12.2.7`, `§12.4`, `§12.5`, `§12.6`, `§11`, `TOC`, and `Projects (§7.3)` / `§7.3` are legacy cross-reference residue. `FinalGUISpec` and FileManager consumers must route to the current FileManager §10 navigation/fallback contract or this LSPSupport section rather than keeping anchors that do not exist.

dimension_assessments.summary: Fallback, chat, lifecycle, crash, phasing, transport, Settings, and worktree behaviors are substantially explicit.
Editor, Chat LSP, fallback, tool operations, and phased capabilities are enumerated.
Inputs and status values are normalized, but operation-specific result payloads and partial/error details are absent.
Protocol, mutation, diagnostic packaging, transport, identity, and surface contracts are stated, notwithstanding the result-envelope gap.
Starting, ready, failed, error, degraded/effective GUI states, and worktree-tied lifecycle transitions are described.
Index, LSP, editor, Search, Problems, status, and Chat authority boundaries are explicit.
FileManager, LSPSupport, Search, Problems, UI, client, and worktree lifecycle ownership are allocated.
Editor, Chat, Problems, Search, status, AI context, and Settings consumers are named with routing boundaries.
Fallback disclosure, Problems/status placement, and the Settings registry's controls and visible states are detailed.
Spawn failure cleanup and crash state cleanup are defined, but restart mode, attempt ceiling, and exhausted state remain discretionary.
Approval gating protects rename, but configurable env fields and stderr-tail logs lack a secret-handling and redaction contract in the reviewed core.
Diagnostics propagate to editor, Problems, Chat, and AI context, while mutations propagate through FileSafe-backed workspace/applyEdit.
Lifecycle, timeout, fallback, transport, and GUI operating paths exist, but crash retry exhaustion and validation execution semantics are not closed.
Debounce and workspace-root caps are concrete, but the open-document eligibility algorithm and default cap are only examples.
Legacy anchors, aliases, transport boundaries, and current owner routes have explicit compatibility treatment.
Phase outcomes supply useful user-visible oracles, but operation result bodies and Settings validation lack executable pass/fail definitions.
Material discretion remains for crash restart policy, document caps, Settings validation, warm-start, and secret handling.
The largest consequential unknowns are result payload shape, retry exhaustion, resource-selection defaults, validation semantics, and sensitive-value handling.
